A.text: A current carrying circular loop of radius R is re-wound into a circular coil of number of turns N. The ratio of magnetic dipole moment of loop and that of coil is
A.sol_text:
Let current in loop is i
So magnetic moment of this loop, M₁ = iπR²
Now if we make N loop. Let radius of loop is r then as length of wire is same
So 2πR = N·2πr ⇒ r = R/N

Magnetic momentum of one loop, M = iπr²
So total magnetic moment of coil,
M_T = N·iπr² = N·iπ(R/N)² = (iπR²)/N

So (M/M_T) = (iπR²)/((iπR²)/N) = N

∴ x = 42

A.text:
Which is the correct sequence for following conversion?

[Benzene ring] → [Benzene ring with CH₃ at top and SO₃H at bottom]
options: [Benzene ring] —(Conc. H₂SO₄)→ [Benzene ring with O inside] —(CH₃Cl, Anhy. AlCl₃)→
[Benzene ring] —(CH₃Cl, Anhy. AlCl₃)→ [Benzene ring with O inside] —(Conc. H₂SO₄)→
[Benzene ring] —(CH₃COCl, AlCl₃)→ [Benzene ring with O inside] —(Conc. HNO₃, Conc. H₂SO₄)→
[Benzene ring] —(Conc. H₂SO₄)→ [Benzene ring with O inside] —(CH₃COCl, AlCl₃)→ —(N₂H₄/OH⁻)→
A.sol_text:
Answer: (2)
Solution:

(1) [Benzene ring] —(Conc. H₂SO₄)→ [Benzene ring with SO₃H] —(CH₃–Cl, H₂SO₄)→ [Benzene ring with SO₃H and CH₃]

During conversion of final product, –SO₃H group acts as m-directing group. So, meta product will be obtained.

(2) [Benzene ring] —(CH₃–Cl, AlCl₃)→ [Benzene ring with CH₃] —(Conc. H₂SO₄)→ [Benzene ring with CH₃ and SO₃H]

Minor + [Benzene ring with CH₃ and SO₃H at para position]

Major product is obtained at para position.

(3) [Benzene ring] —(CH₃–Cl–Cl, AlCl₃)→ [Benzene ring with C(=O)CH₃] —(Conc. HNO₃, Conc. H₂SO₄)→

[Benzene ring with C(=O)CH₃ and NO₂]

C(=O)–CH₃ (i.e., –C(=O)–CH₃) is a meta-directing group. So, meta product will be obtained.

(4) [Benzene ring] —(Conc. H₂SO₄)→ [Benzene ring with SO₃H] —(CH₃COCl, AlCl₃)→ [Benzene ring with SO₃H and C(=O)CH₃] —(N₂H₄/OH⁻)→ [Benzene ring with SO₃H and CH₂–CH₃]

A.subject: Chemistry
A.chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
A.text:
Consider the following organic species.

(I) A benzene ring with a CH₂⁺ substituent
(II) A six-membered ring with an oxygen atom and a CH₂⁺ substituent and an NO₂ group
(III) A six-membered ring with an oxygen atom and a CH₂⁺ substituent and an OCH₃ group

Select the correct statement.
options: II is more stable than III because −NO₂ stabilize the carbocation by resonance effect
I is more stable than II because −NO₂ de-stabilize the carbocation
III is less stable than I because −OCH₃ destabilise the carbocation by inductive effect
II is more stable than I because there is no substituent in I
A.sol_text:
G:ID = 3504408.

Structures shown:
- (I) Benzene with CH₂⁺ and OCH₃ substituent → +R effect
- (II) Six-membered ring with oxygen, CH₂⁺ and NO₂ → −R, −I effect
- (III) Six-membered ring with oxygen, CH₂⁺ and OCH₃ → +R effect

Stability order: III > I > II

OCH₃ is electron donating (through +R effect), stabilizing the carbocation.
NO₂ is electron withdrawing (through −R and −I effects), destabilizing the carbocation.

Therefore, statement (2) is correct: I is more stable than II because −NO₂ de-stabilize the carbocation.

A.text:
Statement-1: On increasing dilution, the conductivity of solution increases.
Statement-2: On increasing dilution, degree of ionization of weak electrolyte increases.

A.text: If |cos x(sin x + √(sin² x + sin² α))| ≤ k, where k ∈ R⁺, α ∈ R and x ≠ (2n+1)π/2, n ∈ Z, then the maximum value of k is
A.sol_text:
cos x(sin x + √(sin² x + sin² α)) ≤ k

Let cos x(sin x + √(sin² x + sin² α)) = t

t = cos x sin x + cos x√(sin² x + sin² α)

(t − cos x sin x) = cos x√(sin² x + sin² α)

SBS and rearranging:

t² − 2t cos x sin x + cos² x sin² x = cos² x sin² x + cos² x sin² α

⇒ t² − 2t cos x sin x − cos² x sin² α = 0

Divide with cos² x,

t²(1 + tan² x) − 2t tan x − sin² α = 0

(tan² x)t² − 2t(tan x) + t² − sin² α = 0

tan x ∈ R

4t² ≥ 4t²(t² − sin² α)

1 ≥ t² − sin² α

1 + sin² α ≥ t²

|t| ≤ √(1 + sin² α)

∴ k = √(1 + sin² α)

A.text: Let f(x) = 1/√x for x > 0, f(1) = 1 and g'(sin²x - 1) = cos²x + K, ∀x ∈ ℝ, g(-1) = 0. If h(x) = {f(x), x > 0; g(x), -1 ≤ x ≤ 0} is a continuous function, then the value of |2K| is equal to
A.sol_text:
f'(x) = 1/√x, x > 0
⇒ f(x) = ∫ x^(-1/2) dx = 2√x + c
⇒ f(1) = 2√1 + c = 1 = 2 + c ⇒ c = -1
∴ f(x) = 2√x - 1

Also, given
g'(sin²x - 1) = cos²x + k, ∀x ∈ ℝ
⇒ g'(-cos²x) = cos²x + k
⇒ g'(t) = -t + k, t ∈ [-1, 0] 0 ≤ cos²x ≤ 1
⇒ g'(x) = k - x, ∀x ∈ [-1, 0]
⇒ g(x) = kx - x²/2 + c₁
where c₁ is the constant of integration

Replacing x by -1
g(-1) = 0 = -k - 1/2 + c₁ ⇒ c₁ = 1/2 + k
∴ g(x) = kx - x²/2 + 1/2 + k
∴ h(x) = {2√x - 1, x > 0; kx - x²/2 + 1/2 + k, -1 ≤ x ≤ 0}
∴ h(x) is continuous at x = 0
∴ h(0) = lim(x→0+) h(x) = lim(x→0-) h(x)
⇒ 1/2 + k = k = -1
⇒ k = -1 - 1/2 = -3/2
⇒|2k| = |-3| = 3

A.text: If a, b, c are in Geometric Progression. and a – b, c – a, b – c are in Harmonic Progression, then the value of a + 4b + c is equal to
A.sol_text:
Answer : (2)
Solution:
a, b, c are in G.P.
Let r is common ratio
b = ar, c = ar²
Now (a – b), (c – a), (b – c) are in H.P.
1/(a – b), 1/(c – a), 1/(b – c) are in A.P.
⇒ (b – c) (c – a), (a – b) (b – c), (a – b) (c – a) are in A.P.
Now (ar – ar²) (ar² – a), (a – ar) (ar – ar²), (a – ar) (ar² – a) are in A.P.
(r – r²) (r² – 1), (1 – r) (r – r²), (1 – r) (r² – 1) are in A.P.
r(1 – r) (r – 1) (r + 1), (1 – r) r(1 – r), (1 – r) (r – 1), (r + 1) are in A.P.
r(1 + r), –r, (r + 1) are in A.P.
Now
–2r = r(1 + r) + (1 + r)
⇒ –2r = (1 + r) (1 + r)
⇒ r² + 4r + 1 = 0 ...(i)
Now value of a + 4b + c
a + 4(ar) + (ar²)
= a(1 + 4r + r²)
= a × 0 = 0

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: The line x + y = 2 intersects the coordinate axes at the points A and B. If a point P(α, 1) lies outside the triangle OAB and inside the circumcircle of triangle OAB, then the complete range of the values of 'α' is
A.sol_text:
Answer: (4)
Hint:
If points O(0, 0) and P(α, 1) will lie on opposite sides of line x + y = 2
⇒ (0 + 0 − 2)(α + 1 − 2) < 0 ⇒ α > 1 and P(α, 1) lies inside of circumcircle
⇒ α < 2

Solution:

[Diagram shows a coordinate system with:
- Point O at origin (0, 0)
- Point A on y-axis at (0, 2)
- Point B on x-axis at (2, 0)
- A circle passing through O, A, and B (circumcircle of triangle OAB)
- The circle has center at (1, 1) and radius √2
- Point P(α, 1) shown on the horizontal line y = 1
- The line x + y = 2 intersecting at A and B
- Labels showing (1−√2, 0), (1, 1), (1+√2, 1), and y = 1]

From the hint, we have two conditions:
1) For P(α, 1) to lie outside triangle OAB: α > 1 or α < 1−√2
2) For P(α, 1) to lie inside the circumcircle: α < 1+√2 and α > 1−√2

Combining these conditions:
- From condition 2: 1−√2 < α < 1+√2
- From condition 1: α > 1 or α < 1−√2

The intersection gives: (1−√2, 0) ∪ (1, 1+√2)

Therefore, the complete range is (1−√2, 0) ∪ (1, 1+√2)

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: A letter is known to have come either from LONDON or CLIFTON; on the postmark only the two consecutive letters ON are legible. The probability that it came from LONDON is
A.sol_text:
Answer : (2)
Solution:
We define the following events :
A₁: Selecting a pair of consecutive letter from the word LONDON.
A₂: Selecting a pair of consecutive letters from the word CLIFTON.
E : Selecting a pair of letters 'ON'.

Then P(A₁ ∩ E) = 2/5; as there are 5 pairs of consecutive letters out of which 2 are ON.

P(A₂ ∩ E) = 1/6; as there are 6 pairs of consecutive letters of which one is ON.

∴ The required probability is

P(A₁/E) = P(A₁∩E)/(P(A₁∩E)+P(A₂∩E)) = (2/5)/((2/5)+(1/6)) = 12/17.

B.text: A normal to the hyperbola x²/4 - y² = 1 has equal intercepts on the positive coordinate axes. If this normal touches the ellipse x²/a² + y²/b² = 1, then 9(a² + b²) is equal to
B.sol_text:
